summary: Chemical_detector codegen, iteration 3. There are two controllers with 19 files, and every requirement is traced. Movement modes now accept a payload-free 'tick' heartbeat, and AvoidingAgain keeps its complementary clock/distance guards.

issues.title: Constant values are not given by the specification
issues.raw: CD-Const1..6 say the values are configured at start-up but give none. Chosen: THR=1.0, LV=1.0, EVADE_TIME=1, STUCK_PERIOD=2, STUCK_DIST=1.0, OUT_PERIOD=1 (durations in Clock units). Small integers keep the waits and clock comparisons small for model checking.
issues.fix_directive: Replace with deployment values if they are known; keep durations small if the model checker's clock range is bounded.

issues.title: Gas analysis ends in a live Concluded state, not a RoboChart Final state
issues.raw: CD-GA-Beh6 ends the analysis ('concludes its search, processing no further readings'). The codegen rules require every mode to have an outgoing transition, so GasDetected goes to Concluded, which keeps accepting gas events: it stores the reading in gs (CD-GA-Var1) but never analyses it and never emits anything again.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm that absorbing readings without analysing them meets 'processing no further readings'.

issues.title: Found idles on tick instead of moving to a Final state
issues.raw: CD-MV-Beh9 (Found -> Final) says the robot stays halted. Found's only outgoing transition is a tick self-loop with no action. flag and the halting move(0, Front) happen only on the transitions into Found, so flag is emitted once.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm that a tick self-loop is an acceptable stand-in for the terminal transition.

issues.title: Invented boundary input 'tick' (platform control-cycle heartbeat)
issues.raw: The spec defines no periodic input. InputEvent.tick is added: a payload-free event meaning 'a control cycle elapsed with no other news'. Every movement mode except AvoidingAgain accepts it as a lowest-priority self-loop with no action. AvoidingAgain is left out because its two autonomous transitions have complementary guards, so one of them always fires. Java behaviour is unchanged, since a mode already ignored inputs it did not handle. The reason for the change is that iterations 1 and 2 timed out in Movement's Isabelle deadlock-freedom proof. The likeliest cause is that states enabled only by the gas analyser's turn/stop/resume events (Waiting, Avoiding, GettingOut, Found) have no provable enabled operation in the per-controller theory.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm that a platform heartbeat is acceptable; otherwise another boundary input must give these modes an enabled transition.

issues.title: analysis/location details not fixed by the specification
issues.raw: CD-Fn1: a reading 'indicates the target chemical' is taken to mean some sensor reports the configured target Chem with intensity > 0. CD-Fn3: angle(x) maps zero-based sensor position x to Angle.values()[x mod 4] (Left, Right, Back, Front), and the first sensor wins a tie. Empty reading defaults: noGas, 0.0 and Front.
issues.fix_directive: Supply the real sensor-to-direction layout and detection criterion if they are known.

issues.title: intensity is the peak over all chemicals, not only the target
issues.raw: CD-Fn2 defines intensity as the maximum i across the whole reading. A strong non-target chemical could therefore trigger stop once analysis has returned gasD. Implemented literally.
issues.fix_directive: Clarify whether the peak should be restricted to the target chemical.

issues.title: Odometer is sampled from the sensor service, not received as an event
issues.raw: CD-Evt3 describes the odometer as a reported distance that the movement subsystem samples into d0/d1. Implemented as Sensor.odometer(), a zero-argument reading fed by Sensor.recordOdometer.
issues.fix_directive: None unless odometer must be an input event.

issues.title: Type realisations for Chem and Intensity
issues.raw: Chem is a record with one nat field (species) and uses record equality. Intensity is a real (double). goreq(i1, i2) is the only ordering the controllers use on it.

issues.title: Operations are platform methods, not compute() classes
issues.raw: CD-OP1..3 (move, randomWalk, shortRandomWalk) are Vehicle-provided actuation, so they are Vehicle methods. CD-OP4 changeDirection(l) is ObstacleEvasion.changeDirection. None of them computes a state variable, so the compute()-style operation class pattern does not fit them.

issues.title: Waiting's during action and the Analysis guards
issues.raw: Waiting's during action randomWalk() runs at the head of the Waiting block on every cycle. Analysis leaves on stsNoGas and !stsNoGas. This is equivalent to sts == gasD because Status has exactly two values.

issues.title: Events a mode does not handle are dropped in Java
issues.raw: Java ignores an event that the current mode does not handle, for example turn in AvoidingAgain or gas while the analyser is in Analysis. Wiring the two controllers together (forwarding actuator outputs) is left to the integrator. It should step the gas analyser with null until it is back in Reading.
issues.fix_directive: Decide whether a system-level integration class is in scope.

next_step: Run the pipeline (compile, coverage, preflight, t2m, m2m, m2t, verifiers) and fix Java from the first failing phase.
